headline: QA-focused Morning Signal — agentic QA, mobile/device streaming, CI/test integration, and AI-for-QA evaluation (2026-10-05)

top_signal.title: Building Reusable Evaluation Frameworks for Agentic AI Products (InfoQ presentation)
top_signal.summary: Susan Chang (Elastic) presents a production-grade evaluation framework for agentic AI: unified benchmarks, combining deterministic rules with LLM-as-judge approaches, and deep tracing to catch agent failures and evaluation drift.
top_signal.why_it_matters: Concrete patterns and tracing practices help QA teams build reproducible agent evaluation, automated failure capture, and metrics suitable for production validation of agentic test workflows.

items.title: Device Streaming and Android skills — available in Android CLI
items.summary: Android CLI adds device streaming and 'skills' for scripted interactions and remote device access, enabling lower-latency debugging and automated tasks against real devices from the command line.
items.why_it_matters: Enables more direct remote access for exploratory and automated mobile testing, shifting how device farms and local debugging integrate into QA workflows and CI test runs.

items.title: Closed-loop incident response: connect AWS DevOps Agent to OpenSearch
items.summary: AWS shows how to connect DevOps Agent investigation events to OpenSearch using the Model Context Protocol to trigger autonomous investigation workflows from alerts.
items.why_it_matters: Automates root-cause triage for test failures and incidents, enabling agents to gather observability context and start investigations that reduce mean time to resolution for flaky or failing tests.

items.title: Stateless GitHub App installation tokens rolled out
items.summary: GitHub completed the staged rollout of stateless installation tokens for GitHub Apps; newly minted tokens now use the stateless format by default.
items.why_it_matters: Test automation that relies on GitHub Apps may need SDK and token-refresh updates; verify token handling in test runners and automation tooling to avoid auth failures in pipelines.

items.title: Copilot code review: API support and new default effort level
items.summary: GitHub added REST and GraphQL API support for Copilot Code Review and changed the default review effort level to 'Balanced', letting tools request programmatic reviews.
items.why_it_matters: QA pipelines can now request automated code reviews for test code and infra programmatically, enabling machine-assisted PR gates and continuous quality checks in test repos.

items.title: TeamCity 2026.2.1 and 2026.1.5 bugfix updates
items.summary: JetBrains released TeamCity 2026.2.1 and 2026.1.5 maintenance updates addressing over 40 security vulnerabilities alongside various bug and stability fixes.
items.why_it_matters: On-prem TeamCity instances used to orchestrate test runs should be patched to avoid compromised CI/test orchestration and prevent downtime that disrupts automated test execution.

items.title: Android Security State libraries enable component-level security verification
items.summary: Google's AndroidX Security State libraries let apps verify security patch status at the component level rather than only a device-wide patch date.
items.why_it_matters: Mobile QA should adapt device gating and security tests to component-level indicators so tests target devices/components with relevant security status and avoid false assumptions.

watch.title: Selected models in GitHub Copilot deprecated
watch.summary: GitHub deprecated several models used across Copilot experiences (completions, agents, chat) as of October 2, 2026, affecting behavior across Copilot features.
watch.why_it_matters: Model deprecations can change automated code-review and generation outputs; QA should monitor Copilot-driven gates and revalidate any tests or heuristics that depend on its behavior.

learning.title: The Platform Engineering Playbook for Production LLMs (InfoQ article)
learning.summary: Article argues treating LLMs as shared platform infrastructure: central observability, platform controls, and guardrails to reduce hallucinations and operational surprises in agentic systems.
learning.why_it_matters: Gives QA teams tactics to design validation, observability, and platform-level tests for LLM-driven features and agent workflows used in production.
